chapter: Lawn parties, excursions and dance-hall work
title: Irish Channel lawn parties and King Foley
summary: Playing for white lawn parties in the Irish Channel where the crowd was given whiskey and fought.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: Oh, lawn parties, we played for white and colored lawn parties. They had, we would have had lawn parties around very often in the place you call the Irish Channel. That's up out front, uptown, out the front, they call it the Irish Channel. They run lawn parties they often. When they hired a band, it was time to knock off and tell you, they got a big .45 pistol and a big quart bottle of whiskey. They said, go ahead and drink now, until you're playing. Until all of them fall on the floor. And they fight, and they cut, then they break it up. We hired till one o'clock. When we leave out there, it's six o'clock in the morning.
Irish Channel. It's still Irish Channel, yeah.
Did you know King Foley? He was the king of the town. Do you remember him?
I heard of King Foley. King Foley, yeah, I heard of him. Name for me is him.
